**Dates:** 30 December 2026 – 8 January 2027

After the celebrations, your journey continues in Búzios, with 5 nights on the tropical coast and several free days. You can explore different beaches, walk around town, take a boat trip, enjoy water sports or simply relax beside the warm ocean without a busy schedule.

## What to expect on your journey

### New Year on Copacabana

On 31 December, Copacabana becomes a vast celebration beside the Atlantic. By evening, the beach fills with people dressed in white. Flowers and gifts are left by the water for the goddess Iemanjá, with wishes for health, love, prosperity and change in the coming year.

Before midnight, Brazilian artists perform on the stages. Fireworks are launched from platforms at sea, rising above the dark water along the length of the beach. The music and celebrations continue long after midnight.

### Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer

You will travel through tropical rainforest to the statue of Christ the Redeemer. From above, you can see Guanabara Bay, the beaches and neighbourhoods of Rio, the green expanse of the Botanical Garden and the slopes surrounding the city. The viewpoint shows how Rio sits between the mountains and the ocean.

### Sugar Loaf

The cable car starts at Red Beach. It first takes you up Urca Hill, then continues to the summit of Sugar Loaf. From here, you can see Copacabana and Ipanema, Guanabara Bay, the Rio–Niterói Bridge and Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado.

### Central Rio

As you travel through the central neighbourhoods, you will see Lapa and the arches of the Carioca Aqueduct, colonial façades, the Metropolitan Cathedral of Saint Sebastian and the colourful Selarón Steps. Old Rio gives you a view of the city beyond its beaches and famous panoramas.

### Búzios

After the busy days in Rio, the trip moves on to a beach stay. Búzios lies on a peninsula with an indented coastline and more than 20 beaches. Conditions vary around the resort: some beaches have calmer water, while others get more wind and waves. In the evening, activity centres on the restaurants, boutiques and galleries along Rua das Pedras.
